title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors and Company Secretary; employees; any other person notified by the Chairperson or Company Secretary that they are subject to the policy; plus, for any of those persons, their Connected Persons (spouse, children under 18, nominee/investment manager) and trusts, partnerships and companies they or their Connected Persons control.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors and the Company Secretary; distinguished only by the 2-business-day deadline to notify the Company Secretary of any change in their (or a Connected Person's) interests in Company securities, so the Company can notify ASX within 5 business days.

tiers.name: Chairperson
tiers.description: Before the Chairperson deals in Company securities (at any time), the Chairperson must obtain approval from at least one non-executive director, instead of from the Chairperson.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Spouse, children under 18 (incl. step-children), nominee including an investment manager managing funds on the Designated Person's behalf, a trust of which the Designated Person or a Connected Person is trustee or beneficiary, a partnership with them, and a company they control.

windows.end_anchor: release by ASX of the Company's Appendix 4E Preliminary final report for the period ended 31 December

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Company Secretary may advise other Prohibited Periods, for example when the Company is embarking on a significant transaction or undisclosed significant development. Confidentiality of such additional periods is not addressed.

rules.detail: Absolute, unqualified ban on trading in derivatives over the Company's securities; no clearance or exception route is provided for this rule specifically (unlike the general dealing rules in 3.4-3.7).
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not trade in the Company's derivatives.

rules.detail: Hedging is not a defined or named concept in this policy; because any hedge of Company shares would require a derivative, and derivatives trading is banned outright, hedging is implicitly prohibited by the same clause.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not trade in the Company's derivatives.

rules.detail: Prepaid forwards, collars sold for premium, or other monetisation structures are not named or otherwise addressed.

Short selling is not named. It is a sale of Company securities and so falls within the general prohibition on dealing while in possession of price sensitive information, the Prohibited Period restriction, and the requirement to obtain Chairperson approval before dealing at any time.
rules.evidence: Before any Designated Person deals in securities of the Company (at any time), they must first obtain approval from the Chairperson.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
A CFD is a derivative over the Company's securities and so falls within the outright ban on trading the Company's derivatives.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not trade in the Company's derivatives.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Granting a charge, lien or other security over Company securities is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Secured financing arrangements in respect of Company securities are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
No minimum holding period or short-term dealing restriction is imposed beyond the general price-sensitive-information and Prohibited Period rules.

clearance.evidence: Each of the directors is required to notify the Company Secretary within two business days after any change in their interests in securities of the Company, or the interests of any of their Connected Persons listed above.

If approval is given, the Designated Person may ordinarily trade within five business days after receiving the approval. ... All other Designated Persons are required to notify the Company Secretary of any dealing in securities of the Company within five business days of effecting such a dealing.
Before the Chairperson deals in securities of the Company (at any time), the Chairperson must obtain approval from at least one non-executive director.

exceptions.evidence: dealing in a managed securities portfolio where the Designated Person is not in a position to influence a choice of the portfolio
conversion of securities on exercise of rights granted under an equity incentive plan
transfers of securities which result in no change in the beneficial interest in the securities
transfers of securities between Connected Persons

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a Designated Person is a trustee, trading in securities by that trust provided the Designated Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Designated Person
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a share purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back
an issue of securities to a Designated Person where shareholder approval for the issue has been sought and obtained in accordance with ASX listing rules

exemption_authority: In exceptional circumstances, the Chairperson may permit a Designated Person to deal during a Prohibited Period; the nature of the exceptional circumstances and the justification must be evidenced in writing (3.4). No waiver mechanism is stated for the separate, absolute ban on trading in the Company's derivatives.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives ban has no clearance route
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not trade in the Company's derivatives.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary share dealing (which can be cleared by the Chairperson), this clause is a standalone, unqualified prohibition with no approval mechanism, so an OTC put and call collar cannot be cleared under this policy at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Before any Designated Person deals in securities of the Company (at any time), they must first obtain approval from the Chairperson. ... This obligation operates at all times.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even outside the annual closed period, any purchase, sale, unwind or physical settlement of a collar's share leg needs fresh Chairperson approval and a written no-inside-information statement each time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance or minimum shareholding requirements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not expressly banned, but granting security over the shares to the bank is not addressed either, leaving real uncertainty over whether it would be treated as a 'dealing' requiring Chairperson approval and, if effected during the annual closed period, a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If approval is given, the Designated Person may ordinarily trade within five business days after receiving the approval. ... A further application will need to be made if no dealing takes place within the five business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared step of a collar (e.g. entry or unwind, to the extent not itself blocked by the derivatives ban) must be executed within a short window or re-cleared, complicating multi-leg execution with a bank counterparty.

summary: A funded collar with a bank is not achievable under this policy. Section 3.3 imposes an absolute, unqualified ban on Designated Persons trading in 'the Company's derivatives' - broad enough to catch an OTC purchased put and written call over vested Neuren shares - and, unlike ordinary share dealing, no Chairperson clearance or exceptional-circumstances waiver is provided for that specific rule. Even setting aside the derivatives ban, any change in beneficial interest in the shares (including any sale to unwind or settle a collar) requires prior written Chairperson approval at all times, not only during the annual closed period running from 1 January until release of the Appendix 4E preliminary final report, and must occur within five business days of approval (two-day notification for directors). The policy is silent on margin lending, secured financing and encumbrance, so the loan and share-charge leg has no express prohibition but also no defined clearance pathway, leaving its treatment as a 'dealing' uncertain. Overall, the standalone derivatives ban is the binding obstacle to a funded collar structure.
